title: Pentagon Ousts Three-Star General, Accuses Him of Leaking Classified War Strategy
snippet: Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was stripped of his Joint Chiefs post after failing multiple polygraph tests regarding leaks about Iran and Ukraine, with the case now referred to the Justice Department.
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has abruptly removed a high-ranking three-star Army general from his post at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, with Pentagon officials accusing him of leaking sensitive military intelligence to the media.

Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, who oversaw strategy, plans, and policy for the Joint Staff, was relieved of his duties late Wednesday. According to a defense official speaking on condition of anonymity, Sylvia failed three separate polygraph examinations during an internal investigation into unauthorized disclosures regarding the war in Ukraine and military operations involving Iran.

DOJ Referral and White House Reaction

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed on social media that the Defense Department took decisive personnel action to safeguard national security intelligence, adding that the matter has been turned over to the Department of Justice for potential civilian prosecution—an unusual step for military personnel typically tried under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

When questioned by reporters on Thursday, President Donald Trump backed the aggressive stance against unauthorized disclosures. "She’s gonna have big problems," Trump said, mistakenly referring to the male officer, before emphasizing, "We’re very much looking for leakers."

Retracted Honors and a Decorated Career

The fallout was felt immediately within the Joint Staff. Initially, officials issued a statement thanking Sylvia for his 32 years of distinguished military service. Hours later, the statement was formally retracted, with spokespeople conceding it "did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances." Sylvia’s official military biography has also been taken offline.

Prior to his assignment at the Pentagon, Sylvia commanded the famed 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. Over his three-decade career, he earned six Bronze Star Medals—including one for valor—along with a Purple Heart for combat wounds.

Broader Crackdown on Military Leaks

Sylvia's sudden departure is the latest in a series of aggressive leak inquiries spearheaded by Hegseth since taking office. The defense chief previously ousted three close aides following a similar polygraph-driven probe and has increasingly restricted press movement inside the Pentagon building.

The removal comes at a precarious moment for military planners, as the administration weighs potential tactical decisions surrounding ongoing Middle East tensions following upcoming congressional midterm elections.
